platforms.name: Browser extension (Chromium)
platforms.notes: 1.5.3 adds an always-on adult-TLD ruleset (`.adult`, `.porn`, `.sex`, `.xxx`) at the published-list priority, so a name registered after the last list build is blocked instead of waiting for a list update. The document rule lands on the block page and every embedded type is dropped; the hand allowlist still wins. `decide` and the open-tab sweep model the same rail, and the static ruleset is pinned by the package check. `.cam` is deliberately not guarded. 1.5.3 also repairs the popup's status render (an undefined reference left the app row, lock strip, notices and details unpainted) and gives the embedded settings the popup's height: five fitting tabs, no pinned full-page footer or language row, a one-tap language switch, and a page area of about 461 px instead of 270. 1.5.2's private-window heartbeat answer, 1.5.1's removal of the browser-side private-window mode and 1.5.0's portable rules are retained.

platforms.name: Mac
platforms.state: development · unsigned, needs Developer ID and notarization
platforms.notes: Build 34 adds the Unrot (general) edition to the Mac app: distraction rules (limits, waits, schedules, Focus, feeds only) with Gentle/Firm/Locked strictness and a weekly emergency pass, an app watcher with a wait/closed panel over the app's window, the Limits and Focus page, the Today page with the sprout, a gold look selected by the HisnEdition Info.plist key, and the bridge's page decisions for the extensions (the extensions do not use them yet). Every target must carry the same MARKETING_VERSION and CURRENT_PROJECT_VERSION. 1.1.18 combines the 1.1.17 work on this branch with the MDM layer: the adult-TLD rail and the craft/extra-sites pass are retained, MDM enrollment is read as its own fact and the Organization policy layer names DEP/MDM versus a local profile, `profile/make_profile.py --mdm --team-id` adds a `com.apple.webcontent-filter` payload (plugin type, socket filter, designated requirement) and a `com.apple.system-extension-policy` that allows the Hisn filter and makes it non-removable on macOS 15+, blocks Erase All Content and Settings, and on macOS 26+ disables Safari private browsing. `HisnProfileVersion=2` and `HisnFilterManaged` let the app leave a profile-owned filter alone, `verify_mdm.sh --strict` checks the layers, and `--maximum` is the supervised-fleet preset. 1.1.16's aggregate blocked-connection count and 1.1.15's Organization Mode are retained. Build 33 restores a full one-minute recovery countdown when a browser is relaunched after a silence closure and, when a browser has no usable native-messaging route, rewrites the user-scope link at launch and while the guard runs before deciding to close anything. Unsigned/unnotarized.

platforms.name: iPhone & iPad
platforms.state: development · no Apple team or test device; direct IPA path built, unsigned
platforms.notes: The app, six Safari blockers, HisnDNSProxy, HisnActivityMonitor, the scanner and two shield extensions share one version set. 1.8.0 adds the device-wide DNS filter: a Network Extension DNS proxy answers the signed core tier (236,586 domains), the four adult TLDs, 116 hostname terms and the person's saved sites with a local NXDOMAIN, and forwards only allowed names to Cloudflare Families over HTTPS. Domain and term data are generated from the signature-verified seed at build time and checked again by SHA-256 at start; a damaged domain list stops the extension instead of running unfiltered. The app gains on/off, readback, a route self-check through a reserved hisn.invalid alias and a commitment freeze. The old NEDNSSettingsManager Family DNS configuration is removed and the app entitlement moves from dns-settings to dns-proxy. 1.8.0 also adds the direct distribution path: ios/direct/build_direct.sh packages an IPA outside the App Store and make_source.py writes the AltStore source from its bytes. Simulator-tested only; the DNS extension, the permission prompt and the direct install need a signed device. 1.7.2's adult-TLD Safari rules, 1.7.1's weekday quiet hours and 1.7.0's pause rule are retained.

platforms.name: Android
platforms.state: beta · 1.0.0-beta1 / 44, signed direct APK; desktop and emulator tests only, no phone acceptance run
platforms.notes: 1.0.0-beta1 (44) is the first public beta. The version name restarts at 1.0; the build number continues from the 1.6.0 (43) development candidate, so an installed 1.5.x or 1.6.0 build updates in place. It carries the 1.6.0 candidate (see docs/ANDROID_1.6.0.md) plus the phone-maker setup screen, the wait-before-opening rule, the onboarding checks page and the matcher performance pass (docs/ANDROID_FILTER_PERFORMANCE_2026-11-14.md). The 1.6.0 record's limit still holds: the dashboard can read disconnected after a reboot, and no phone acceptance run is claimed. The app runs on Android 6.0 (API 23) and later; image checks remain Android 14+.
